# ARGUS UI standards: the owner's picks

> Picked by the owner on 2026-09-28 on the standards picker. One standard per role. GENERATED from `apps/portal-frontend/js/ui-library/registry.json` by `scripts/ui-library/standards-md.mjs`; edit the registry, not this file.

⛔ Standing rules: never change Financials unless told; charts stay different from each other (only font, text and axis are shared); Employees does not change; keep the Financials timeline ruler; the empty tick box is grey in dark mode and white in light mode; the illustrated default faces stay.

- Kit note, 'Argus suggests' to-do panel: The standard is the kit's existing Kit.guide, unchanged. Default is three made-up steps, most urgent first, each in its own box: a number badge (amber for today, the accent for this week, plain for a good idea), the words, and the one quiet button that does it. Hover, focus and pressed land on the first step's button, which wears the kit's shared focus ring. Empty is all caught up, which a page may only say when the reads behind the list came back with nothing. Error is a read that failed, and says so; it never says all caught up. Busy is the reads still out: a quiet clock, no count and no steps. Compact is its size for a narrow rail, where the button drops under the words, as it does on a phone. The steps slide in and the tick pops the first time the panel is seen on a visit, at the kit's panel duration; with reduced motion on (the computer's setting or Settings > Preferences) nothing moves. The library draws every other cell at rest and plays the entrance once in its own cell. A real step is only ever built from a real read.
- Kit note, Could-not-load message: Copied into the kit from Financials' failed chart, which is unchanged. A flat plate in the neutral fill Financials' module skin gives it (a light grey in light, white at 6% in dark), with one centred sentence in the second ink and, when the read can be asked again, one Try again. Try again is the kit's everyday button, the same outlined button the source draws: a named button that darkens under the pointer, wears the kit's shared focus ring (the source's own is a thin wine glow) and takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. The plate takes the height of what failed; the library gives it a boxed chart's 296px. Default is the plate drawn with the page, which is not announced. Error is the same plate after Try again failed again: it appears after the person did something, so it is an alert and is read out at once. Empty is Financials' quiet-period note: no plate, the sentence on a small raised note at 38% of the chart it lies over, which keeps its zero; the chart under it here is a stand-in, not a chart. Bare is a failed read that cannot be asked again. The words are made up.
- Kit note, Empty state ('nothing here yet'): The standard is ArgusTable's own empty, failed and loading messages, unchanged, on made-up rows. Default is empty: the table keeps its header and its shape, five still ghost rows fade out under a scrim of the page, and one centred sentence sits over them; no icon, no box, no pill. The action variant adds one quiet button under the sentence. Error is a failed read: the sentence in full ink and an outlined Try again, and no rows at all, not even stale ones. Busy is the rows as breathing bars; with reduced motion on they hold still. Hover and focus land on Try again: its hairline and words darken under the pointer, and it keeps ArgusTable's own red focus ring rather than the kit's shared one, because it is an existing kit part and is not retuned. The empty sentence is a polite status. ArgusTable marks every failed read an alert, including one drawn with the page; that is unchanged here.
- Kit note, Good news message (done, all clear): Copied into the kit from Settings Team's 'done' line, which is unchanged. A green tint and hairline, a green tick, the words in full ink and a Dismiss cross. Bad is the same line for an action that failed: the red tint, the red hairline and a red warning glyph, as the source draws it and the picker showed it. It does not move. The line's live region is mounted once and stays in the page, rendered and empty, until something happens; each outcome is written into it, so a screen reader hears it: good news is a polite status, a failed action an alert. Hidden is that: the region mounted with nothing in it, which takes no room (the library outlines the place it keeps). The cross is a button named Dismiss, a 26px square that goes to full ink under the pointer and when pressed; it wears the kit's shared focus ring (the source's sits 1px out) and takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. When it puts the line away, keyboard focus goes to the place the page names, or to the element the line sits in, rather than being lost. The source puts good news away by itself after six seconds; the kit leaves that to the page. The page places it: the source's 12px under-margin is the page's.
- Kit note, Inline notice (info, warning, error): Copied into the kit from Financials Transactions' notice line, which is unchanged: the owner's pick is that line, the first row of the picker's card. A sentence about the list under it in full 14px ink on the neutral fill Financials' module skin gives it, with the skin's hairline and 8px corners. It may carry one quiet text button after the words (the kit's quiet button, the source's Financials text button) and a round Dismiss cross in the line's own ink, with the neutral fill under the pointer. Warn is the skin's amber fill, hairline and ink, for something that needs a look. Hover, focus and pressed land on the button; the x variants on the cross. Both wear the kit's shared focus ring and take the 44px floor on a touch screen, and dismissing the line hands keyboard focus to the place the page names, or to the element the line sits in. The line's live region is mounted once and stays rendered and empty until show() writes into it, so a screen reader hears it; both tones are a polite status (the source makes its warn tone an alert). Hidden is that empty region. Settings Team's grey banner, which the family's first brief named, is not this part and is unchanged. The page places it: the source's 12px under-margin is the page's.
- Kit note, Page explainer at the top: The standard is the kit's existing help banner, unchanged, placed the way Financials places it today: 4px under each tab's own head row (the tab's name and one sentence), through the kit's slot, which holds one banner for each place. Its doors are the other tabs. Showing a banner replaces the one already there, a banner other code left in the same place goes too, and a claim taken before a slow load draws nothing once its tab has closed. So each tab shows exactly one banner, under its own heading, and switching tabs puts the new tab's banner in place of the old one; the switched variant is the Spending tab switched to Revenue with nothing torn down, and it still holds one banner. There is no new kit class for it. Hover and focus land on the first door: it lifts under the pointer and wears the banner's own focus ring, the same 2px accent outline as the kit's shared one; its two state rules now also answer the library's forced state, and nothing a page shows changed. Below 760px across the doors go and the words take the width. The banner rises in the first time it is seen on a visit, at the kit's panel duration, and holds still with reduced motion on; the library draws it at rest. The head row here is Financials' own, for context.

- Kit note, Drop a file here: Copied from Inventory's Scan an invoice window (.invscan__zone, css/inventory-scan.css:251-349, js/inventory/invoice-scan-modal.js:518), which is unchanged: a dashed well on the recessed ground with 16px corners, the drawn box and arrow, what to drop at 14px/600 and a caption. Under the pointer, and while a file is held over it, its line and mark take the module's colour (Inventory's teal, drawn here with Inventory open; the kit accent outside a module) and the fill lifts to the chip grey. The well is lit by the kit's one drop helper, the same one the profile photo and the logo square use: it lights up only for a drag that carries files, counts the drag in and out so crossing the words inside does not flicker it, and hands every file dropped to onFiles. Its drag-over look is the helper's .is-drop, where the source's is .is-over. The keyboard way in is the well itself, a real button (the source's is a div with role button): Enter, Space or a click opens the file picker, and the picker and the drop hand files to the same onFiles. A refused file is a red sentence under the well, read out at once and tied to the well as its description; the next files clear it. Checking the files is the page's (the source refuses a type, a size and a count), so the page calls refuse() with its reason. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not the source's red one. Off (not in the source) is dimmed like the kit's buttons and takes nothing: a file let fall on it is still caught (the drag is cancelled and says it takes nothing), so the browser never opens it over the page, and nothing lights up or is handed on. The teal line is a thin state line on a light fill, under 3:1 in light, as the source draws it; the words say what the well is in both themes.
- Kit note, Search and filter bar above a list: The standard is the layout and spacing of Financials Transactions' bar (.ftx-bar, css/financials-transactions.css:61-81, js/financials/view-transactions.js:722), which is unchanged: the search field, the in-page switch and the filters in use on the left, 8px apart; the dates and the filter buttons on the right, the last action 4px further apart; the two sides wrap under each other, 12px apart, when the row runs out of room. It draws none of the parts it holds: each is the kit's own standard, as it is. The search box is Kit.searchField, the All / Money in / Money out segments are Kit.inlineSwitch, the dates are Kit.rangeButton, Filters, View and Export are Kit.filterButton (Export with no pop-out), and a filter in use is Kit.filterChip, set, with its x. So their looks are those standards': the source's joined grey segments are the in-page switch's white chosen segment (the pick's pressed segment is the switch's chosen one, and the switch draws no separate press), and a tag is the filter chip's wine tint where the source's is grey. Filters in use is the filter button's own .is-on (Filters (1)); open is the filter button's own open fill. The filters in use sit in a group named 'Filters in use', which takes no room when there are none. Keyboard focus is each part's own, which is the kit's shared ring.
- Kit note, Photo or logo picker: Owner: the illustrated default faces stay. The picture is Kit.personPicture's (the people-media family's picture), so a person with no photo of their own shows their illustrated face (assets/avatars/face-NN.svg, picked from their id), the initials if it fails to load, and their photo only when they uploaded one; the page passes photo only then. Copied from the Account page's photo (.account-avatar-wrapper, css/account.css:40-93, js/account.js:139), which is unchanged: a 76px rounded square with 16px corners and the account page's strong line, and over it a 55% black veil with a camera and CHANGE in 11px caps. The source's veil is out of reach of the keyboard: nothing in it takes focus. Here the veil is a real button, named 'Change photo', that Tab reaches; it shows under the pointer and while it has keyboard focus, wears the kit's shared focus ring, and opens the file picker. On a touch screen the veil stays out of sight and a tap on the photo opens the picker, as the source's does.
- Kit note, Saving and saved note: The kit's one save note: Kit.settingRow (the toggles family's setting row) draws this one, so a row and a hand-made slot say saving in the same words and look. Copied from SettingsUI.status (js/settings.js:1335) and .sf-status (css/settings.css:784-832), which are unchanged. Default is idle: empty, and it takes no room. Busy is 'Saving…' in the grey, with aria-busy on the row. Saved is green with a small tick and fades after two seconds, over the kit's exit fade (180ms) where Settings takes 400ms; the words go when the fade ends. The library holds saved still, and draws the fade's end. Error is 'Couldn't save. Try again.' in red with an underlined Retry, which stays until it is fixed; refused is the same red with no Retry ('Only an admin can do this.' unless the page says why). The note is a live region: a polite status, an alert while it says a save failed or was refused. Retry is a real button that calls the page's retry bare; hover and focus land on it. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not the source's own; on a touch screen Retry is at least 44px square.
- Kit note, Bar that appears when rows are ticked: Copied from Financials Transactions' bulk bar (.ftx-dock and .ftx-bulk, css/financials-transactions.css:865-930, js/financials/view-transactions.js:2773), which is unchanged. The dock is sticky at the foot of the list and takes no height, so ticking a row never moves the list; on it sits a centred island, 52px tall, 8px corners, the raised surface with the strong line and the deep shadow, rising into view over the source's 180ms (not under reduced motion). The library pins the dock in its cell. How many are ticked in 14px/600, then the actions, each the kit's everyday button (buttons__everyday), where the source draws its own 36px outlined buttons: so they are 32px with 15px words, and under the pointer their line and words darken rather than filling grey. The island is a region named for what is ticked, and the count is a polite live status, so a screen reader hears '5 selected' as it changes; the words go in a moment after the island comes up, so the first count is heard too. Nothing bookable ticked is the page leaving Categorize out. Busy is the island shrunk to 'Booking 2 of 5…' while the booking runs, marked busy; focus that was on an action goes to the page. Focus on an action stays in the bar when the actions are drawn again: on the same action, or the first one when it is gone or has no key; with no actions left it goes to the page. announce: false writes the count at once (a page drawn with rows already ticked); the library draws its cells that way. Escape does not clear the selection, as in the source. Hover, focus and pressed land on the buttons; keyboard focus is the everyday button's, the kit's shared ring.
- Kit note, Undo after removing something: Copied from Settings > Quiet time's undo (.qt-undo and .qt-textbtn, js/settings/quiet-time.js:1359-1463, css/settings/settings-alerts.css:47-79 and :725-739), which is unchanged: 'Cleared your quiet hours.' at 12.5px in the grey, then Undo at 13px/600 in the accent ink, a word button with 6px corners that takes the faint accent tint under the pointer and while pressed. The two sit 6px apart, where the source has 2px, so the shared focus ring (4px outside the button) clears the sentence's full stop. It is not Kit.notify's action look (that is the quiet grey button, 15px), so Undo has its own. The sentence and its Undo sit in a polite live region that stays on the page (empty, it takes no room), so both are read out as they come. The offer goes after eight seconds, as in the source, but waits while the pointer is on it or Undo has focus; a new offer replaces the last. Pressing Undo takes the offer away, calls the page's undo, and puts focus back where the page says (or on the element the sentence sits in), never on nothing. The library holds the offer still. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, where the source draws its own accent ring; on a touch screen Undo is at least 44px square.

- Kit note, Bar chart over time: Not copied into the kit (owner: charts stay different): the library draws it with Financials' own code, window.FinCharts (js/financials/charts.js, painted by css/financials-charts.css), in the page's skin (.mod-skin > .fin-frame, Financials open), and neither file is changed. The figures are made up, six months up to the library's fixed day. The chart is mounted once it is on the page, because it measures the width it is given (620px here). Its hover tip is the module's own, which it puts on the page fixed to the window; the library's page of charts scrolls, so the library holds the tips in one layer over the page and moves the place the module works out onto the page (css/ui-library.css .uil-tips, and the window reads as tall as the page while the library drives it, so a lower cell's tip is not pulled up to the window's floor). Default is money out by vendor: Wholesale grocer, Payroll, Rent and Snack distributor take the four named colours (--crm-cat-1..4) and Everything else the fifth. Hover is April under a real pointer move, through the chart's own handler: the grey band behind the column, the April label in bold, and the tip with every vendor and the total. Keyboard focus is the chart holding the real focus, which draws the module's own ring (its :focus-visible outline in --crm-focus, not the kit's shared ring, which stays with kit parts) and opens its first column. A frame opened on its own (as the local check opens it) takes that focus at once. Inside the library page a frame never takes the page's focus by itself: its focus cell opens its first column and tip through the module's own focus handler, and takes the real focus, and with it the ring, when the pointer comes into its frame. All cashflow stacks money in up and money out down. A vendor toggled off is the legend's own button, clicked: its swatch greys and its layer goes. Unavailable is money in not known: the plate and the reason, never a zero line. The chart grammar is the one thing every chart shares (owner: charts look different, and the font, the text and the axis are the same): the kit's chart tokens, --kit-chart-font and --kit-chart-label-size for the labels, --kit-chart-axis for the axis and the hover line, --kit-chart-grid for the grid and --kit-chart-tip-ground, -ink and -line for the hover tip. No chart reads them yet; moving each chart onto them is rollout work, and until then the charts keep their own sheets. The grammar cell is the library's own drawing of those tokens, not a chart.
- Kit note, Small trend line on a card: Not copied: it is the chart inside the kit's own figure card, Kit.balance (js/kit/balance.js, the balance card section of css/kit.css), drawn by that code and unchanged; the tiles family shows the same card as a card. Thirty made-up days up to the library's fixed day, drawn at rest (on a page the line draws in the first time it is seen). A monotone area: a 1.75px line and a faint fill, no grid, a hairline axis with four dates. Hover is a real pointer move at a point on the plot, through the card's own handler: the 1px rule, the hollow ring and that day's figure, date and change in the header. Keyboard focus is the card's own ring round the plot (the module's colour, the kit's existing hook for this part) and the arrow keys walked five days back, through the card's own keyboard handler. The card picks its size from its own width: compact in the state cells (340px), standard and large in the variants. Falling is a series that ends lower (the red arrow); one point shows No history yet and no chart; not loaded shows no chart. The shared chart grammar (--kit-chart-*) is shown on the bar chart; this chart does not read it yet.
- Kit note, Heat maps and one-off charts: Not copied into the kit (owner: charts stay different): the library draws it with Financials' own code, window.FinCharts (js/financials/charts.js, painted by css/financials-charts.css), in the page's skin (.mod-skin > .fin-frame, Financials open), and neither file is changed. The figures are made up, six months up to the library's fixed day. The chart is mounted once it is on the page, because it measures the width it is given (620px here). Its hover tip is the module's own, which it puts on the page fixed to the window; the library's page of charts scrolls, so the library holds the tips in one layer over the page and moves the place the module works out onto the page (css/ui-library.css .uil-tips, and the window reads as tall as the page while the library drives it, so a lower cell's tip is not pulled up to the window's floor). Default is all cashflow: four made-up sources flow into Money in (green ribbons), the money out leaves it for Expenses and fans out to the vendors (dark red ribbons), with a thin node bar at each end and the name and amount beside it. Hover is Inside sales under a real pointer move, through the chart's own handler: that flow lit, the rest dimmed, and its tip with its share. Error is a read that failed: the plate and Try again, no marks. - Kit note, Bars in a list or table: Not copied into the kit (owner: charts stay different): the library draws each bar with Financials' own FinCharts.shareBar (js/financials/charts.js, painted by css/financials-charts.css), in the table it lives in, Financials' breakdown (.fi-bd, css/financials-insights.css), in the page's skin, Financials open; none of those files is changed. The rows and amounts are made up. A 4px grey track in the % of total column; each row's slice starts where the row above it ended, so the column reads as a staircase that adds up to 100%. Dark red for money out, green for money in. A tiny share takes the 2px floor and a zero share draws no fill. Default only: the bar has no hover or focus of its own. The row's grey tint under the pointer is the breakdown table's (a plain :hover on .fi-bd__row.is-link), which the library cannot force without copying Financials' CSS, so it is not drawn here; the kit's own copy of that table, Kit.lineTable (tables family), shows its hover. The shared chart grammar (--kit-chart-*) is shown on the bar chart.
- Kit note, One bar split into parts: Not copied into the kit (owner: charts stay different): the library draws it with Inventory's own code, the pure healthBand that Analytics > Reports mounts (js/inventory/analytics.js, painted by css/inventory-analytics.css, its empty card by css/inventory-order.css), in a .kit.inv-sub page with Inventory open; neither file is changed, and nothing is read from Inventory's API. The counts are made up. Drawn at rest (on a page the bar draws in and the count counts up once). The count that needs attention and of how many, one 12px rounded bar split into critical (red), low (amber) and healthy (green) with 2px gaps and a 3px floor, then a dot key with counts. No hover and no focus: it is a picture with its counts in words (role img, named). Empty is a catalogue with no stocked items and its one way on, Add an item; many need attention and all healthy (one segment) are the variants, and not in the answer is the card that says so. The shared chart grammar (--kit-chart-*) is shown on the bar chart; this bar does not read it yet.
- Kit note, Line chart over time: Not copied into the kit (owner: charts stay different): the library draws it with Financials' own code, window.FinCharts (js/financials/charts.js, painted by css/financials-charts.css), in the page's skin (.mod-skin > .fin-frame, Financials open), and neither file is changed. The figures are made up, six months up to the library's fixed day. The chart is mounted once it is on the page, because it measures the width it is given (620px here). Its hover tip is the module's own, which it puts on the page fixed to the window; the library's page of charts scrolls, so the library holds the tips in one layer over the page and moves the place the module works out onto the page (css/ui-library.css .uil-tips, and the window reads as tall as the page while the library drives it, so a lower cell's tip is not pulled up to the window's floor). Default is cashflow: straight lines with a dot on every month, money in (green) above zero and money out (dark red) mirrored below it, on the dotted field, with the $K axis on the left, the months under it and the toggle legend under the plot. Hover is April under a real pointer move, through the chart's own handler: the hairline and the boxed tip with both series. Keyboard focus is the chart holding the real focus, which draws the module's own ring (its :focus-visible outline in --crm-focus, not the kit's shared ring, which stays with kit parts) and opens its first column. A frame opened on its own (as the local check opens it) takes that focus at once. Inside the library page a frame never takes the page's focus by itself: its focus cell opens its first column and tip through the module's own focus handler, and takes the real focus, and with it the ring, when the pointer comes into its frame. Here the keyboard also takes one step right, to February, through the chart's own arrow keys. Busy is the dotted field alone (it shimmers on a page); empty is a measured zero line with its sentence over it. One direction is money in alone; a series toggled off is Money out's own legend button, clicked: the button muted and the line gone. The shared chart grammar (--kit-chart-*) is shown on the bar chart; this chart does not read it yet.

- Kit note, Filter chip: Selected is the chip with its filter set: the wine tint, no edge, full ink. The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the soft wine halo round the whole chip this chip draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere, drawn round the button that has focus, which is the chip, or the x on its own when the x has it. It opens what it is given in a pop-out, the way the filter button does: one pop-up open at a time, Escape, a click outside, and one Tab that closes it and moves on. In the pop-out Up and Down move from control to control, and a choice list counts as one, with Left and Right moving its choice; the chevron flips while it is open, and the x gives way to it, as in Financials. The pointer over the x is over the chip too, so the x takes its deeper tint on the chip's own hover tint, as in Financials, and the library shows both. The source has no off look; the kit dims the whole chip to half, and it does not light up under the pointer, whether it was switched off or its button was given aria-disabled. On a touch screen the chip and its x are 44px tall and the x 44px across.
- Kit note, Number badge (counts and changes): Named kit-number-badge beside the kit's older Kit.count, which is unchanged: the pick sets its words on a taller line (line-height 1.4) and goes to the full ink on the selected tab, which Kit.count does not. Selected is the badge on the selected tab: the lighter grey and the full ink. Needs a look is the pick's warn tint; all clear and critical, which other screens show as green or solid red, are the same shape in the ok and bad tints, as your picker note asked for an unread count. A tone keeps its colours on the selected tab. A count nobody could read (no number) hides the badge rather than showing a zero. The library draws it beside a tab's words; it takes no pointer and no focus of its own.
- Kit note, Label on a picture or chart: Default is a camera's name with no state, in the plain grey. It sits on video, which is dark in both themes, so the label looks the same in both. Live is the green dot, and it pulses; with reduced motion on (the computer's setting or Settings > Preferences) it holds still. The dot paints no words, so it is an image named Live for a screen reader. Demo is a camera on sample footage: the plain grey label, reading Demo. The dashboard's old LIVE and DEMO pills (solid wine, solid amber) are a different look and are not this one. It takes no pointer and no focus.
- Kit note, Pick chip (choose options): Picked from Settings: the alert channel chips (Email, Text, In the app) and the days of the week, one look in two sizes. The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the accent ring this chip draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. Choosing any number, each chip is a toggle button (aria-pressed) and its own tab stop, as in Settings; the arrow keys also move along the row. In a setting row the group takes the row's words as its name, and each chip keeps its own. Just one is the same look on the radio pattern, as the kit's pick-one list: one tab stop, the arrow keys move the choice, Space chooses, Enter does nothing. Always on is Settings' locked In the app chip: dashed, not a choice, and not dimmed, so it stays readable; a screen reader hears its words and "always on". It is for choosing any number only: in a pick of just one it would be chosen for good, so there the kit warns and draws an ordinary choice. Settings has no off look for the other chips; the kit dims a chip that is off to half, whether it is off by disabled or aria-disabled, and neither answers a click, Space or Enter. The day letters are named in full for a screen reader. On a touch screen each chip is 44px tall, and a day 44px across.
- Kit note, Plain tag (names a thing): The outline, the corners and the type are the Financials category tag's. The coloured outlines are the Loss prevention badges' (Not rung, Rung), which already use the kit's colours; Financials' own warn and danger tags are the same idea a shade off in dark mode, and the kit keeps one set. A status belongs on the status tag; this one names a thing. Narrow table is the 18px size that ends in an ellipsis. It has no browser tooltip with the whole words, since the kit draws none; a screen reader still reads them whole. It takes no pointer and no focus.
- Kit note, Status tag: The kit's status tag, picked as it is and unchanged: 6px corners, no edge, a soft tint, and the colours ease when the status changes. Default is the neutral grey (mut), which is what Kit.pill gives when no tone is passed. It takes no pointer and no focus.

- Kit note, Loading placeholder (grey bars): Copied into the kit from Financials Insights' breathing bars, which are unchanged. A flat bar in the chip grey (Financials' --ground-chip, which the kit already had), 6px corners, no box and no shimmer, where a figure or a line of words will go, never a zero. It breathes between 55% and full every 1.2s, the source's pace written as five of the kit's panel durations; under reduced motion (the computer's setting or Settings > Preferences) it holds still at full. The sizes are the source's, named for what each stands in for: hero 140 x 28 (a headline figure), figure 96 x 22 (one beside it), stat 56 x 18 (a summary grid's figure), total 110 x 14, cell 70% x 12 and amount 80px x 12 at the right edge (a table's words and money), and line (a line of words, short for the last one). The bar is hidden from a screen reader; the region it stands in says it is busy. It is now the kit's one loading bar: Kit.figureRow's loading figures and Kit.lineTable's loading and empty rows are drawn with it (both had their own copy of the same Financials bars; the empty table's rows hold still), so default here is Financials' headline figures still loading, drawn by Kit.figureRow. Rows is a money-in breakdown still loading, its header kept over seven rows; lines is a paragraph. ArgusTable's own loading rows are an existing kit part and keep theirs. The library draws the bars at rest; on a page they breathe.
- Kit note, Figure we can't show yet: Copied into the kit from the Dashboard's KPI wall, which is unchanged. An en dash in the figure's own place, never a zero, at the figure's own size and weight (it takes both from the slot it is put in; the library's slot is the Dashboard KPI's 34px bold), in the Dashboard's lighter ink, and when the page knows why, a small line under it that says so. The dash reaches 4.9:1 on a white card and 7.2:1 on the dark one, and the words 4.5:1 or better on the page and on a card in both themes. Error is a read that failed: Did not load and Try again, Financials' quiet word button in the full ink that underlines under the pointer and when pressed; it wears the kit's shared focus ring (Financials' own is a soft wine glow), set 8px from the words so the ring stands 4px clear of them, and takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. Hover, focus and pressed land on Try again. Inline is the same failed read in a Financials summary cell, the words beside the dash. Cell is a table cell nobody measured: the dash alone. A screen reader hears the dash as Not known, or Not loaded, or the name the page gives it. It is now the kit's one missing-figure dash: Kit.figureRow, Kit.plainFigure, Kit.statusFigure and Kit.lineTable draw theirs with it. Transactions' tooltip on its dash is the browser's own, which the kit never draws; a page that needs the reason on a table cell's dash names it (the label) or puts the kit's hover tip on it. The labels, the figure slot and the table are the library's; the words are made up.
- Kit note, Notification pop-up: Copied into the kit from the app's global notification (showToast, css/main.css:2785-3024 and js/main.js:11497-11685). ⛔ main.js's toast is the source and is unchanged, and the library frame never loads main.js, so this is a copy: a later step of the rollout makes showToast call Kit.notify, so the app has one notification. It sits top-centre under the header, stacked 10px apart, at most 640px across: a raised card (white in light, #232323 in dark) with a hairline and a heavy shadow, a 26px glyph in the tone's colour, the words in the full ink at 16px and a round Dismiss cross. The glyph colours are the ones main.js writes inline, which win in both themes (blue, green, amber, red); the words carry the meaning, and in light the green and amber glyphs are under 3:1 on white, as picked. It stays 3.5s, 5s for a warning and 7s for an error, unless the page says otherwise (0 keeps it); the count stops while the pointer is on it or focus is in it. The same words in the same tone twice within 3s show once. Its message (the title and the words) is a live region, a polite status and an error an alert, and the words are written just after it goes in, so a screen reader hears them; the action and the cross sit outside it, so they are not read with the message. The cross is a button named Dismiss, a 36px circle that washes under the pointer and when pressed; it wears the kit's shared focus ring (the source's is a 2px ring in the glyph's colour) and takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. If focus was in it when it goes, focus moves to the stack it sat in, or where the page says. It drops in on a spring at one and a half panel durations and lifts out at the kit's exit duration, with the source's own curves, and the ones under it glide up; under reduced motion it simply appears and goes. Title is the heading with the words as a quieter detail line; action is one quiet button (Undo), which also puts it away. Loss Prevention's app tag (showToast's app option) is not part of this pick and is not drawn. The library puts each one in its cell rather than the page's stack, and keeps it until dismissed; open is the drop-in, which plays once as the frame loads, and leaving is the lift-out frozen halfway, as the picker drew it (a look only the library draws). The words are made up.
- Kit note, App opening screen: Copied into the kit from the boot screen (#nexus-loading-screen), which is unchanged: index.html's first paint is inline and draws before the kit has loaded, so it stays there. This is the same lockup for any other screen that has to wait before it can draw. The Argus mark with a soft red halo breathing behind it every 2.6s (Kit.standaloneMark, busy: the icons family's mark, the on-light art in light), ARGUS in wide tracking, a 168 x 2px track with a red segment sweeping along it every 1.3s, and a caption that says what is happening. The paces are the source's, written in the kit's durations; the curves are the source's own. The caption is a polite status, so a screen reader hears each step (caption: Signing you in); the mark, the word and the bar are hidden from it. No ground of its own: the page shows through, and the page places it (index.html's is a fixed layer over the whole screen). Under reduced motion (the still variant) the halo and the bar hold still, the segment parked a third of the way along as the source parks it, and only the words change. leave() fades it out at the kit's exit duration and takes it away; that is a fade to nothing, so it is not drawn. At rest the segment sits where reduced motion parks it, so a still frame never reads as a bar a third full. The wordmark's face is the source's stack (Lexend Peta, which the app does not load, so the system face shows, as on the boot screen).
- Kit note, Progress bar: Copied into the kit from the invoice scan window's file rows, which are unchanged. A 4px rounded track (a mid grey) and two claims that never look alike. Default is a MEASURED bar, a file being read (42% here): the fill grows from the left in the module's colour, Inventory's teal here (the frame opens Inventory; outside a module it is the kit accent), it is a progressbar with its value, 0 to 100, and the words say the amount too (Reading the file · 42%); a screen reader has the amount from the bar, so the amount in the words is hidden from it and the live words are not read again at every step. Busy is the scan itself, which reports nothing about its progress: no fill, only a segment travelling along the track every 1.15s, and a progressbar with no value, which is how a screen reader is told the amount is unknown. At rest the segment sits mid-track, never at the start, where it would read as a measured fill. Queued draws no bar, only the words (Waiting its turn). Error is a file that could not be read: no bar, the words in the failed ink (the second ink in light and a soft red in dark, as the picker drew them) and the ways on, the kit's small 28px buttons, the size the scan window draws. The words under the bar are a polite status, so each step is heard. Every bar has a name (the file). Under reduced motion (the still variant) the travelling segment becomes a still 45% tint of the whole track. The fill keeps the picked teal: on the light track it is under 3:1, and the words carry the amount, as the bar's value does. The file row around it (the name and the size) is the library's; the file names are made up.
- Kit note, Spinner, loading words or busy button: Copied into the kit from Employees' certificate reading and Loss Prevention's clip review, which are unchanged. A 26px circle with a 2.5px ring in the second line colour and its top arc in the kit's wine, one turn every 0.8s at an even speed, centred over one sentence in the full ink, and, if the page has one, a quieter line of detail (the detail variant). It is a polite status with the sentence in it, so the sentence is what a screen reader hears; the ring is hidden from it. Video is the same sign over a clip, which stays dark in both themes: a faint white ring with a deep wine arc and white words. ⛔ Under reduced motion (the computer's setting or Settings > Preferences) the ring slows to one turn every 1.6s, as picked, and never stops, because a still ring says nothing is happening; the kit says so with its own two rules, since main.css stops every animation under the preference and spares only classes named spin, and the kit names nothing spin. The library draws the ring at rest; a still frame cannot show a turn. The reading box and the clip stage are the library's; the words are made up.

- Kit note, Code or address with Copy: A new kit part, Kit.copyBox, copied from Settings' new API key box (css/settings/settings-system.css:346-373 and js/settings/api-keys.js:138-167), which is unchanged. The picker listed Kit.modal, but the dialog is only where Settings puts the box, so the box is its own part and sits in a dialog or anywhere else. The words, whole, in a raised mono box with 8px corners that selects as one piece, beside the kit's button (kit-btn) with the copy glyph. The words are a read-only field named by textLabel that takes keyboard focus, and keyboard focus selects them, so Cmd or Ctrl+C copies them without a pointer; their ring is the kit's shared ring, the same 2px accent Settings draws. The button's name is its words, whatever they say (Copy key, Copied, Select it and copy), so what a screen reader reads is what is shown; Settings names it Copy the new key, which does not hold its words. The field's name (The new API key) describes the button, from a hidden line of its own, never from the key, which would read the key aloud. A press puts the words on the clipboard through the one copy helper the copy icon shares: the browser's clipboard, else a selection and the browser's own copy command. Copied turns the button's word, glyph and hairline the kit's green (--kit-ok, --kit-ok-line) for two seconds, the hold the kit's Saved uses; blocked says Select it and copy and selects the words for the person to copy themselves. A screen reader hears Copied or Could not copy from the part's own polite live region. The green clears 4.5:1 on the button in both themes (5.2:1 light and 7.0:1 dark, at rest and under the pointer). The button takes the 44px floor on a touch screen, as every kit button does.
- Kit note, Small copy icon: A new kit part, Kit.copyIcon, copied from Financials' trend note copy (css/financials-insights.css:395-442 and js/financials/view-insights.js:2278-2296), which is unchanged. A 32px raised square (the hairline, the surface and the one-layer lift Financials' skin gives it, which is the could-not-load note's lift, the same value in both themes) with the 15px copy glyph in the quiet ink, the ink under the pointer and while pressed. Copied swaps the glyph for a check (both Kit.glyph's) for two seconds, through the one copy helper the copy box shares: the browser's clipboard, else a selection and the browser's own copy command. A screen reader hears Copied or Could not copy from the part's own polite live region; that is how a blocked copy is told, and the icon itself does not change, as the source. The check stays in the ink, as picked: the green is the copy box's. With reveal, as in Financials' note, it waits for what holds it: out of sight until the element it sits in is under the pointer or holds keyboard focus, and always in sight on a touch screen, which has no pointer to wait for. The note's grey band is the note's, not the icon's. Its name comes from the page (label: Copy section). Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not Financials' translucent red one. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen.
- Kit note, Section that folds open: A new kit part, Kit.foldOpen, copied from Financials Transactions' Show graphs chevron (FinControls' bare icon button, css/financials-controls.css:374-426, and css/financials-transactions.css:666-675), which is unchanged. A 32px square with the 16px chevron in the second ink: no box at rest, the chip grey and the ink under the pointer and while pressed. At rest and under the pointer it is the icon button's look (kit-icon); it is its own part because its open is not the icon button's (which keeps the chip grey while its menu is up): open, the square stays bare, as Financials' does, and the chevron turns to point up on the kit's duration, so reduced motion stops the turn. It is a disclosure: aria-expanded says open or shut and aria-controls names the section it opens, whose hidden follows it. Its name is the section's and stays (label: Graphs): Financials swaps Show graphs and Hide graphs, which says the state twice. Off is dimmed with no chip grey and the plain arrow. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not Financials' translucent red one. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen.
- Kit note, History list: A new kit part, Kit.historyList, copied from Loss Prevention's alert history (.inc-timeline, css/argus.css:12314-12418), which is unchanged. A mono uppercase label (a heading, at the page's level) over a real ordered list (role=list, because list-style none takes a list's meaning away in Safari), one step to an item: the kit's status dot (icons__status-dot: its 7px disc and its tones, where LP's is 6px) in a rail with a hairline down towards the next step, then what happened, who did it in the ink, and when in mono, a <time> carrying its datetime when the page gives an ISO date or date-time (anything else, such as yesterday, says so and is shown as words with no datetime); what they wrote sits under the line. The dot is hidden from a screen reader: the words say what happened. LP colours its dots by status, and the page gives each step a status dot tone: confirmed theft bad (red), escalated warn (amber), not theft the plain grey, and under review and opened info, the status dot's blue, which is LP's own (icons__status-dot). The hairline above the block and the red left edge are the alert drawer's, not the list's. Each step rises in on the kit's kit-enter, not LP's staggered 0.3s, and holds still under reduced motion. LP's quiet words are the kit's ink-3, which clears 4.5:1 in both themes (LP's dark meta is 42% white, under it). Empty is an alert nobody has touched yet.
- Kit note, Keyboard key hint: A new kit part, Kit.keyHint and Kit.keyHints, copied from the search window's footer (.search-footer-hints, css/dashboard.css:10713-10739, and index.html:3565-3570), which is unchanged. The kit's one keycap: a <kbd> in 10px mono on the key fill, with a hairline and 4px corners, in the shell's muted ink (the pop-up search's key tokens, reused); beside its words (11px, the same ink) it is a line, and a row of lines sits 14px apart. The pop-up search's esc (inputs__popup-search) is this keycap now, so the kit has one. AI on is the same row with the Ask AI hint; the red ARGUS AI ready at the footer's right end is the search window's own sign, not a key hint, and is not part of this standard. The keycap's ink clears 4.5:1 on its fill (5.5:1 light, 5.1:1 dark), and the words on the footer's ground (5.0:1 light, 5.6:1 dark). It takes no pointer.
- Kit note, Show more / See all: A new kit part, Kit.showMore, copied from Settings' Show every step (.sa-disclose, css/settings/settings-apps.css:181-218, and js/settings/recognition.js:284-296), which is unchanged. 13px semibold words in the accent ink with a small chevron after them, 6px apart; the words underline under the pointer and while pressed. It is a disclosure, as the fold open is: aria-expanded, and aria-controls on the section it opens, whose hidden follows it. Open, the words become the page's open words (Hide the steps) and the chevron turns to point up on the kit's duration, so reduced motion stops the turn. The chevron is Kit.glyph's at 14px, where Settings draws a rotated border. Off is dimmed, with no underline. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, the same 2px accent Settings draws. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. The steps table under it is the page's (Kit.table), not part of this standard.

- Kit note, Icon backing (bare or on a tile): The standard is the kit's icon button, kit-icon (the buttons family's Financials bare icon button), unchanged: Settings draws its glyphs bare, with no tile or disc behind them, and that is what the icon button already is. A 32px square around a 16px glyph in the kit's one line style (Kit.glyph, icons__line-style): no box at rest, the chip grey under the pointer and when pressed, off dimmed to half with the plain arrow for a cursor, and keyboard focus in the kit's shared ring. The glyph is hidden from a screen reader and the button carries the name (aria-label), so a glyph that is the only thing in a button is named by the button. Settings' own seven copies of the glyph helper stroke at 1.8 and are unchanged; the kit draws every glyph at the line style's 1.7. Quiet hours' square remove button turns red under the pointer; that red is not the bare icon, and the icon button keeps the chip grey. Word is the same bare glyph inside a word button, as Settings Team's Invite draws it: a 14px plus before the word in the kit's primary button. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen.
- Kit note, Line icon style: Copied into the kit from Financials' icons (js/financials/controls.js:198-283, view-insights.js:141-148 and .fc-ico, css/financials-controls.css:35-58), which are unchanged. One helper, Kit.glyph, draws every glyph: path data on a 24-unit grid, stroked in the ink of whatever it sits in, 1.7 wide with round caps and joins, never filled. The 1.7 is in the glyph's own grid, so it scales with the glyph rather than holding a fixed pixel width (no vector-effect): 20px is the 16px glyph drawn larger, as Financials draws its 14px and 16px glyphs. Three sizes, 14, 16 (the default) and 20; a part that draws at another size keeps its own, and its own size wins. The named set is Financials' 34 control glyphs, the filled checkCircle (the wine disc with its tick knocked out in white, as Financials and the side tabs draw it) and the Insights glyphs, Settings Team's warning triangle, the app notification's four circled glyphs (circleInfo, circleCheck, triangleAlert and circleX, which are line glyphs, so they joined the set), and close and back, the kit's own words for x and chevronLeft; a page may pass its own path data, and a name that is not in the set (a typo, or 'toString') draws nothing and says so. A glyph is always hidden from a screen reader and never takes focus: a button that holds only a glyph is named by its aria-label. Every glyph the kit's newly picked parts draw now comes from this one helper in this one style, so these changed weight: the full screen's close and arrows (2.25 before), the search box's and the pop-up search's magnifier and the sign-in field's tick and cross (2; the pop-up's own larger magnifier is the set's now), the dates button, the filter button, the good-news line's glyphs and Dismiss cross, the back link and the menu inside a page (1.8), the health score's arrow (1.6), and the notification's four glyphs and its cross (2; their drawings are the set's now). Five marks stay heavier because their picks draw them so: Financials' own dropdown and filter-chip chevrons and the chip's x at 2 (the Financials look's own rule), and the tick in a tick box (3), a pick chip (2.6) and a saved setting row (2.4). The parts that were in the kit before these picks (the dropdown's chevron, Kit.searchBox's magnifier, the checkmark, the sparkline, charts, the balance card, the help banner and the guide) are unchanged. A glyph has no state of its own: it takes the ink of what holds it, so the bare icon (icons__icon-backing) shows the button's.
- Kit note, ARGUS logo in page headers: Copied into the kit from the top bar's logo (AxTopBar, js/system/topbar.js:295-336, and css/topbar.css:53-105), which is unchanged. The 26px mark and the 14px wordmark, 9px apart. Both artworks ship and the kit's stylesheet shows the one for the theme, so flipping the theme needs no rebuild; without that sheet all four images show. It is a real link home (the top bar's is a button), named ARGUS home; the four images say nothing of their own. A plain click can be the page's own (onClick); a modified one (a new tab) stays the browser's. Nothing changes under the pointer or when pressed, as the source. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not the red square outline the top bar shows today. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen.
- Kit note, ARGUS mark on its own: Copied into the kit from the boot screen's mark (#nexus-loading-screen, index.html:296-330 and :633-641, and its light swap, css/shell-theme.css:5949-5951), which is unchanged: that first paint is inline and draws before the kit has loaded. A 48px mark in a 64px box: the white-disc mark in dark and the black-disc on-light mark in light, which reads a little larger, as picked. Default is the mark standing alone, an image named ARGUS for a screen reader; beside its own word it is hidden instead. Loading (busy) puts the soft red halo behind it, breathing every 2.6s at the source's pace and curve; under reduced motion (the computer's setting or Settings > Preferences) it holds still at the source's resting glow, and the library draws it that way, frozen. Kit.openingScreen now draws its mark with this, so there is one copy of the boot mark in the kit.
- Kit note, Status dot: Copied into the kit from Settings' flat dots (.tp-dot, css/settings/settings-team.css:456-474, and .sd-dot, settings-devices.css:119-133), which are unchanged and already drew with kit tokens. A 7px disc, flat, no halo, 7px before its words; default is the kit grey, with Settings' own words for each tone (Active, Expired, Offline, Invited, Removing). A dot never carries the meaning alone: beside its words it is hidden from a screen reader, which reads the words, and standing alone it is an image with a name (alone: Online). A dot given neither says so and is named in plain words for its tone (Status: warning, Status: off), never the tone's code; an unknown tone says so and draws the grey. Pulse is Documents' intake dot (css/documents.css:1826-1852): it grows and fades in turn every 1.1s, the source's pace written in the kit's durations; under reduced motion it holds still, beside its words (the still variant) or on its own. Info is the history family's blue, a matter still open, as Loss Prevention's alert history draws under review and opened (--kit-status-dot-info, its own #1d4ed8 light and #93c5fd dark; 6.1:1 on the light page and 6.7:1 on a card, 9.4:1 and 8.7:1 in dark), with Settings' pattern of words beside it (Under review). Against the page and a card, every tone clears the 3:1 a shape needs in both themes (the lowest, the accent on a dark card, is 4.7:1) except muted, Settings' hairline grey: 1.3:1 on the light page and 1.5:1 on a dark card, as picked. Its words say what it means. The camera label's live dot (chips__overlay-label) is not this dot: it sits on video in both themes, with its own green, ring and 2.4s pulse, and is unchanged. It takes no pointer and no focus.

The underline no longer turns ink on focus: the ring marks it. The tick, the cross and the message use the kit's timing, so the tick no longer overshoots as it appears.
- Kit note, Box inside a table row: The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the one this box draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. A text box with a number keyboard (inputmode="decimal"), not the browser's number field, so it shows no up and down arrows: the kit ships no native number control.
- Kit note, Text box: The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the one this box draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. The amber line under Financials' date pair belongs to the date pop-up, not to the box, so it is not part of this standard.

- Kit note, Back link: Copied into the kit from the Settings menu's Back to home row, which is unchanged. A real link with its words: a chevron in a 36px box and the words in the full ink, 13px at 550, 32px tall, 8px corners, drawn at its authored size (Settings sits in the shell's rail, which is drawn at nine tenths, so there it measures 29px). Under the pointer a light wash; in light the words turn the dark red the shell gives every link under the pointer, which is what the owner saw. Pressed is the hover, as the source's is. Keyboard focus wears the kit's shared ring, not the source's thin blue inset line. A plain click can be the page's own (onClick); a modified one (a new tab) stays the browser's. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. In a collapsed menu (Kit.sectionMenu's back option) it is the chevron alone, and under the pointer or keyboard focus the chevron's box takes the wash and its name comes up in the menu's dark banner, which a screen reader does not hear twice. The ground and the width in the library are the Settings menu's.
- Kit note, Main side menu: Not copied into the kit: the portal has one main side menu, the shell's rail (js/system/rail.js and css/rail.css), and there is only ever one, so the library draws that one with its own code, as the shell does, and a screen must not build a second. It is live only where the new chrome is switched on (feature_chrome_v7). Default is its open look with Review current; hover, focus and pressed land on Financials; selected is Financials current. Collapsed is the rail's own collapse (its arrow turns round, as the app draws it); the library puts back the collapse choice the rail writes to the browser, so drawing it changes nothing for the portal. Its hover shows the rail's own name banner beside Financials. The rail's hover and ring are plain :hover and :focus-visible, which the library's forced states cannot reach, so the library repeats the rail's own declarations on its forced cells only (css/ui-library.css); the rail's sheet is untouched. Its ring is the rail's own red one, 2px set 1px out, not the kit's shared ring, and its rows keep their 34px, with the rail's own 44px floor on a touch screen (css/chrome-v7.css).
- Kit note, Page title: Copied into the kit from Financials' page title, which is unchanged. The kit's name leaves out the word page on purpose: the shell recolours any heading inside a class that says -page. An h1 in Inter 28px 600, and 10px under it a 40 x 3px bar in the wine that draws in from the left, which the stylesheet draws, so a screen reader hears only the title; under reduced motion it is simply there (the Bar drawn in full cell; the default cell may be caught while it draws in). A quieter 13px sentence under it (the looks note said 14px; Financials renders 13px). Always the 10px: Loss Prevention's page reset takes it away, which puts the bar through the bottom of its first letters. Colours as Financials renders them in both themes: the title in the shell's ink and the sub line in light the shell's forced paragraph grey (5.2:1). Actions, when a page has them, sit at the right. The words are Financials'.
- Kit note, Section heading: Copied into the kit from Financials' head for each tab, which is unchanged. An h2 in Inter 20px 600 in the full ink, one plain sentence under it in the quieter grey at 13px (the looks note said 15px; Financials renders 13px), and 16px of room under it. With its one action is the same head with the section's one action at the right, as Spending carries Export (the kit's wine button). The words are Financials'.
- Kit note, Menu inside a page: Copied into the kit from the Settings menu with search and groups, which is unchanged; the other modules' menus inside a page will use it. A nav named for its section, on the Settings rail's own ground: the back link, the bold title, a search box named for a screen reader, then each group's uppercase eyebrow over a list of real links, 32px rows of a glyph (the page's own path data) and a word in the quiet grey (drawn at their authored size; Settings' rail draws them at nine tenths). Under the pointer a wash and the full ink (the dark red in light, as the shell draws every link); pressed is the hover. The chosen row is aria-current=page, in 600 weight, its glyph and words red on a red tint. ⛔ The dark words are lifted to #ff8585: the source's #ff3131 is 3.0:1 on its tint, under the 4.5:1 a 13px word needs; the glyph keeps the red. The placeholder is at full strength (the source's 80% is 3.2 to 3.4:1), lifted in dark to 5.0:1. Keyboard focus wears the kit's shared ring, drawn inside the row because the rows sit 1px apart, and round the search box while its words have focus (the source's is a thin blue line). Tab walks the back link, the search box and the links in order. The search filters as it is typed in: every word must match a row, its keywords or its group; a group with no match goes. A polite status line says how many match, or No settings match “zebra”., which is also the one grey line shown in place of the list (empty). Esc in the box clears it and goes no further while there is something to clear; Enter opens the first match. Collapsed it is a 52px column of glyphs: the title and the search go, each eyebrow is a short hairline (its words stay for a screen reader), each link keeps its name, and the glyph's box carries the wash, the chosen tint and the ring; under the pointer and on keyboard focus the row's name comes up in a dark banner butted against the menu's edge, as Settings' does, which a screen reader does not hear twice. The rows, the back link and the search box take the 44px floor on a touch screen. The groups shown and the width are the library's (five of Settings' groups).
- Kit note, Skip to content link (keyboard only): Copied into the kit from index.html's skip link, which is unchanged, for the pages other than index.html (the library's own page carries one). A real link, out of sight until it has focus (the first Tab), then a red tag 10px in from the top left of the window with white 14px words, 4px corners, pointing at the page's main landmark. Keyboard focus wears the kit's shared ring, not the source's white outline. ⛔ Two fixes on the pick: in dark the source's #ff3131 puts its white words at 3.7:1, under 4.5:1, so dark is #dc2626 (4.8:1); and in light, under the pointer, the shell turns every link's words the same #8a1f1f as the fill, so the words vanish (the picker's focus + hover cell): the kit's words stay white. It takes the 44px floor on a touch screen. The stand-in page in the library is the library's.

- Kit note, Full-screen view or page cover: Copied into the kit from the Documents viewer, which is unchanged. The whole window on the page ground with no scrim, fading in over the kit's short duration (1ms under reduced motion). The head holds the large close on the left (44px, as the owner asked for in Documents), the name and a line under it, and the previous and next arrows on the right; the left and right arrow keys step too, as in Documents, but not in a field, a control that uses those keys, or a list open over it. At either end of a list set() turns that arrow off (disabled, its key with it), and focus on it moves to the other arrow or the close; the document sits on a recessed stage with the panel beside it, and on a narrow screen the panel goes under it. It is a modal dialog named by its name: focus moves to the close and stays inside, the page scroll is locked and the page behind is inert, Escape closes it and focus goes back to what opened it (or to returnFocus), all undone on close, and the page's live regions stay live; it takes part in Kit.closeAll. Hover, focus and pressed land on the close and both arrows, which wear the kit's shared focus ring and take the 44px floor on a touch screen. The page on the stage and the panel's contents are stand-ins (a blank sheet, a tag and two kit buttons). In the library it is drawn as a still copy inside a window-sized box in its cell: the real one opens, is copied and closes at once, so it never covers or traps the frame.
- Kit note, Hover tip: Copied into the kit from the Dashboard's KPI chart tip, which is unchanged: near-black with a faint hairline in dark, near-white in light, 7px corners, the Dashboard's ink. The owner's rule: charts keep their own hover cards, and this is the tip for labels, icon buttons and everything else. A line of words is 12px; the chart tip's three lines (the day, the heavy figure, a note) are kept for a tip that reads like one. The Dashboard's foot-traffic tip is not copied: its words go dark on its dark card in light mode. The tip meets WCAG 1.4.13: it opens under the pointer and on focus, so a tap opens it too; it stays while the pointer moves onto it (the chart tip it is copied from lets the pointer through, this one does not); Escape puts it away without moving the pointer or the focus and closes nothing else, not even the dialog it sits in. It describes its trigger (aria-describedby, role tooltip). A word that explains itself goes in the tab order with the dotted underline and the kit's shared focus ring, and on a touch screen a 44px box around it. In a box that scrolls or clips (a pop-up window's body, a table), a tip that would be cut off is lifted out and fixed to the screen beside its trigger, above it or, with no room, below it. It fades in over the kit's short duration, 1ms under reduced motion. The headline figures' label tip (Kit.figureRow) now wears this look, in its own place above the label. The balance card's badge tip is its own and is unchanged.
- Kit note, Dropdown menu and pop-out panel: The standard is the kit's one pop-out shell, kit-pop-out, and nothing new was copied for it: Kit.buttonMenu, Kit.filterButton and Kit.filterChip open it (the toolbar dropdown's list wears it too), and it is already the picked Financials menu, measured against it in both themes: the same fill, edge, 12px corners, shadow and 150ms scale-in from 0.97. Every cell is Financials' Saved views menu under its button. Hover rests the pointer on a row: the ink wash comes up and its rename and delete come out. Focus is the keyboard on a row: a plain row with the kit's shared focus ring round all of it, rename and delete inside it, not the wash Financials shows (a row action the keyboard is on draws its own ring). Selected is the chosen row, heavier words and the wine tick. Disabled is a row that is off: dim words, no wash, the plain arrow. The rows are out of the tab order and the arrow keys, Home and End walk them; one Tab closes and moves on, Escape closes the innermost pop-up only, a click outside closes it, only one is open at a time, and a pop-up opened from inside it keeps it open. The table's sort menu is ArgusTable's own and is unchanged. Words are made up.
- Kit note, Pop-up window: Copied into the kit from Inventory's form window, which is unchanged. Kit.modal is not this look (22px corners, a flat scrim, a ruled head), so it keeps its own and this is a new name. A 12px box over the dark scrim, 640px wide (720 lg, 760 xl), left aligned, the title, a line under it, the form, and the actions on a hairline: Cancel with the field edge and no fill, the confirm in wine with white words. The fields are the kit's text boxes under the source's semibold 12px labels, in its two-column grid. Hover, focus and pressed land on both buttons, which wear the kit's shared focus ring and take the 44px floor on a touch screen. Disabled is the window busy: both buttons at half strength. Error is a save the store refused: the red line at the top, which is always in the page and empty until it has something to say, and the field it names, whose edge takes the window's red (3:1 against the field in both themes; the text box's own refused tint does not reach it and is unchanged outside a window) with the reason under it, tied to it by aria-describedby and aria-invalid (setFieldError). It is a modal dialog named by its title and described by its line, or by its sentence when it is a sentence: focus moves in (the first field) and stays in, the page scroll is locked and the page behind is inert, Escape or the scrim closes it and focus goes back to what opened it (or to returnFocus; opened from a menu row, which goes with its menu, to the menu's button), all undone on close. The page's live regions (the announcer and the toasts) stay live under it. It takes part in Kit.closeAll, and a list opened from a select inside it keeps it open. The rise is the frame's scale-in over the kit's short duration, 1ms under reduced motion. The purchase order's x is the kit's icon button. The source's step-by-step form (NexusUI.stepper) is not part of the window. In the library it is drawn as a still copy inside its cell: the real one opens, is copied and closes at once, so it never covers or traps the frame. Words are made up.
- Kit note, Side panel: Copied into the kit from Financials Transactions' floating detail sheet, which is unchanged. Named kit-side-sheet, not the proposed kit-side-panel: the shell repaints any class with "panel" in its name. 400px, 12px in from the top, the right and the bottom, the pop-out shell's fill, edge, corners and shadow, which are the sheet's own; it slides 12px in from the right. No scrim: the page beside it stays in use, so it is not modal, as its source is not. It is a dialog named by its title, focus moves into it and goes back to what opened it (or to returnFocus), and its x (the kit's icon button) or Escape closes it; it traps nothing, locks nothing and leaves the page live. Escape is the page's first, as in its source: the sheet takes only an Escape nothing else wanted, not one a list or a field handled, not while a list or pop-up is open anywhere, and not a box with words in it. One at a time: a second takes the first one's place. It takes part in Kit.closeAll. An amount raises its cents, as Financials prints one. Hover, focus and pressed land on the x and the link, which wear the kit's shared focus ring and take the 44px floor on a touch screen. Its status tag is the plain grey tag, as picked. In the library it is drawn as a still copy over a stand-in page. Words are made up.
- Kit note, Yes/no question: The standard is the kit's existing Kit.confirm, unchanged. Default is the question as it opens, Cancel holding the focus (the safe answer first), with no ring because a pointer opened it. Hover, focus and pressed land on both buttons, which wear the kit's shared focus ring. It is an alert dialog named by its title and described by its sentence; focus stays inside it, Escape and the scrim both answer no, and focus goes back to what asked. In the library it is drawn as a still copy inside its cell: the real one opens, is copied and closes at once, so it never covers or traps the frame. Words are made up.

- Kit note, Live camera picture: Named kit-camera-view, not the proposed kit-camera-tile: a class with 'tile' in it is repainted by the shell. Copied from the Ops TV wall's tile (css/argus-ops.css:7433-7584, js/argus-ops.js), which is unchanged: graphite, a 1px line, 8px corners and a 16:9 stage that shows the whole frame. The Ops console is dark only and the picture is video, so it looks the same in both themes, and every --kit-camera-view-* token is one literal in both blocks. The name-and-status line draws no label of its own: the camera's name is Kit.statusDot's words beside its dot (the icons family's dot, hidden from a screen reader beside its words), and what the camera is doing is Kit.overlayLabel (the chips family's label on a camera picture), moved out of the picture's corner into the line. The dot takes the label's on-video colours (green live, amber snapshot, red lost, grey while connecting), because the page's tones are too dark on video in light mode. The state is always in words as well as colour: Connecting in the label's own blue connecting look, Live in the label's live green (its dot's, on the label's words), Snapshot in its amber reconnecting look, as the source's green MJPEG and amber SNAPSHOT pill do, and VIDEO LOSS at the size of the picture with its reason under it, where the label is left out, as the source leaves out its pill. The source's pill named the video's transport (MJPEG, or three dots while connecting); the kit's label says the state by default, and a page may give it its own words (label: 'MJPEG'). The factory hands back { el, setState }: setState(state, label) moves one view through connecting, live, snapshot and lost as the stream does, keeping its picture. The live dot holds still: the source breathes it, and the kit's dot pulses only for work in progress. A camera that opens is a real button named for it and its state ('Aisle 4: Live'); it is busy (aria-busy) while it connects. Under the pointer the line lightens and the view lifts, as the source's; a lost camera keeps its red line. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not the source's own. Large is the wall focused on one camera: a bigger name and a taller line. On a phone the source drops the pill and the reason; the kit keeps both.
- Kit note, Clip or alert thumbnail in a list: Copied from LP overview's recent-incident frame (.ov-rc-thumb and .ov-rc-play, css/argus.css:10104-10190, js/argus.js), which is unchanged: a 168px 16:9 frame with 8px corners, the picture cropped to fill on LP's sunken ground (--kit-still-ground, the module skin's #f3f4f6 and #171717). The play mark is the bare white triangle with a drop shadow, not the square mark the tables use; it is drawn with Kit.glyph from its own path and filled, as the line style's one filled glyph is, and it shows only while there is a clip to play. A frame that opens a clip is a real button (a link, with href) named after the clip; one that opens nothing is hidden from a screen reader inside the row button that does. Empty is the source's pruned clip: the slate wash the module skin turns the maroon into, and, unlike the source, the words 'Clip no longer available' on it and no play mark, because there is nothing to play. A frame that fails to load turns empty. The source outlines the frame while its row is under the pointer; the kit does it while the frame, or the button or link holding it, is. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring round the frame, not the source's red ring round the row.
- Kit note, Large saved picture (evidence, keyframe, page): Copied from LP's tracked-person dossier (.trk-entry-media and .trk-entry-gone, .trk-clip-thumb, .trk-media and .trk-drop__img, css/argus.css:10632-10877 and :12983-13021), which is unchanged. One saved picture in four sizes: a log entry's 88px 16:9 photo (7px corners), a clip picker's 16:9 frame as wide as its card (7px), the evidence still (the full width, up to 420px tall, the whole picture shown, 12px corners and a hairline) and the upload preview (a 62px square, 8px corners, on the neutral wash). A photo is cropped to fill; the evidence still is shown whole. All sit on LP's sunken ground: the log entry's source paints --argus-bg-deep, which never turns light and draws a black box on a white page (the source's own comment says so), so the kit uses the sunken ground its pruned entry already uses. Empty is said in words in every size: 'Clip no longer available' (a log entry), 'No frame saved' (a clip with no frame), 'Picture no longer available' (the evidence still), 'No picture' (an upload). The words are the kit's quiet ink: the source's --dim is 2.6:1 in light and 3.3:1 in dark, under the 4.5:1 small words need. The picture sits in its box (the box is the part, the picture inside it), so a picture that fails to load turns the box empty whether or not it is on the page yet; it listens for the failure before its source is set. It takes no pointer and no focus; the picker card's Attach and the upload's Remove are the page's own buttons.
- Kit note, Logo, product and file square: Copied from Settings > Store's logo (.sst-logo, css/settings/settings-store.css:193-216, js/settings/store.js logoRow()), which is unchanged and already drew with kit tokens: a 52px square with 12px corners, a 1px kit line on the second surface, two initials 17px/650 in the second ink. A logo covers it, and one that fails to load puts the initials back. Initials are the first and last words' first letters, or a one-word name's first two (the kit's one rule, Employees'); with no name it shows the store glyph, never a '?'. While a file is held over it (the kit's one drop helper, which the file drop well uses too, sets and clears .is-drop), a dashed accent line on the accent tint. It lights up only for a drag that carries files, not words or a link, and it counts the drag in and out, so crossing the picture or the letters inside it does not flicker it. With onFile it comes with its keyboard way in: a real button beside it ('Choose a file' in the kit's .kit-btn, as Settings draws Upload logo, or the page's own button as chooser) that opens a file picker behind it, and the picker and the drop hand a file to the same onFile. Beside a row label (the default) it is hidden from a screen reader, which reads the label; standing alone (alone: true) it is an image named for the store (a logo carries the name as its alt text). It takes no focus of its own.
- Kit note, Person picture in lists and the top bar: Copied from Employees' picture (.emp-av, css/employees.css:758-775 and :2441-2477, js/employees/ui.js avatar()), which is unchanged. Owner: the illustrated default faces stay. Default is one of the 24 CC0 faces Employees ships, drawn from the same files (/assets/avatars/face-NN.svg) and picked from the person's id exactly as Employees picks it, so one person has one face on every screen; they are shipped files, never fetched from DiceBear. Under it are the initials, which show when the face (or a photo) fails to load; a photo covers the circle. Nobody named yet is a dashed circle with the kit's thin person glyph. Initials are two letters 600 in a dark hue on a pastel of the same hue that stays light in dark mode. Employees derives that hue from the name and paints it inline; the kit paints no colour from JavaScript, so the hue band (35 to 325, never red) is cut into twelve pastels, each carrying its centre hue's literals, and a name keeps one of them everywhere. Every tint's letters clear 4.5:1 (they are 10 to 24px at 600, which is not large text): Employees' formula falls to 4.26:1 near hue 60, so the yellow-green twelfth's ink is taken from 32% to 31.4% lightness (#67742c, 4.53:1), the one departure from the formula. Beside a name it is hidden from a screen reader; standing alone (alone: true) it is an image named for the person. It takes no pointer. The profile photo picker with the illustrated faces (bars__photo-picker, account.js) is a separate standard and is not this picture.
