- Kit note, Scrollbar: A new kit class, copied from the View options scroll area (.avs-scroll, css/argus-view-settings.css:173-181 and :545-549; the clip review's evidence panel has the same rule, css/argus-clip-workspace.css:673-680), which is unchanged. No track: a 9px bar whose thumb is a 5px pill (a 2px clear edge each side) with round ends, in the ink at 20% in light and white at 14% in dark (--kit-scrollbar-thumb), so it follows the theme. It is the same pill on a sideways bar. The source has no hover or drag look, and a class cannot force the browser's scrollbar into one, so default is its one state, as the spec says. Chromium, Edge and Safari draw the pill; Firefox has no way to draw it and shows its own thin bar in the same colour. A scrollbar colour set further up the page (Loss Prevention sets a red one on its whole page) would stop Chromium drawing the pill, so the class sets its own back to the default. The pill is a quiet hint, 1.5:1 against the box in both themes, as picked; the list and the wheel are how a person scrolls it. The box, its title and the rows are the library's.
- Kit note, Sideways scrolling row: A new kit part, Kit.sidewaysScroll, copied from the page tab row's hidden bar (.crm-tabs, css/argus-crm.css:1826-1834) and the Dashboard's app carousel (css/dashboard.css:353-367), which are unchanged. The row scrolls sideways under a trackpad, a wheel or a finger and shows no bar at all; past the edge it is simply cut off, with no fade and no arrow, because the picked source has none (only the Financials timeline fades its ends, and that is not this pick). It is one row of whatever it holds, 8px apart. The kit's own tab rows (Kit.mainTabs, Kit.subTabs) already scroll this way; this part is for any other row. The keyboard can always reach it: a row that runs past its edge with nothing inside that takes focus (the tags here) takes focus itself, as a region named by its label, so the arrow keys scroll it, and it wears the kit's shared ring, rounded to the row's 8px corners. A row that fits has nothing to scroll and takes no Tab stop. It decides again whenever its size changes (a ResizeObserver, let go once the row leaves the page) and when the page calls kitSync(). A row of buttons or links (the Buttons variant, Settings' team filter) takes no focus of its own, since Tab reaches each button and the browser scrolls the row to show it. The row keeps 4px of room inside its edge, taken back outside, so a ring on it or on a button in it is not cut off. Scrolled is the same row part way along; the library scrolls it once the cell is on the page. The tags and words are made up.
- Kit note, Slider: A new kit part, Kit.slider, copied from the clip review's seek bar (.acw-scrub, css/argus-clip-workspace.css:421-468 and :1882-1895, js/argus-clip-workspace.js:1629-1665), which is unchanged. It is a kit control, not the browser's range input, so the part of the clip that has loaded can be drawn behind the part that has played. A 5px bar with rounded ends: the track white at 13%, what has loaded white at 20%, what has played in the wine (#a8293f), and a 13px white knob with a dark shadow that grows to 15px under the pointer and while it is dragged. The review screen is dark in both themes, so the slider brings its own strip, the transport's dark ground (#181818, --acw-panel) with 12px above and below and 16px at the sides, and reads the same on any page in either theme; every colour is one literal in both blocks. The strip's 8px corners are the kit's; the source's transport runs edge to edge. It is a slider with a name (Seek), its ends and where it is, which a screen reader hears as time, 0:12 of 0:30. Left and Right (and Down and Up) step it 1s, Page Down and Page Up 10s, Home and End go to the ends; the source has only the arrows. The pointer drags it with the pointer held, so a drag that leaves the bar still ends where it is let go, and pressed is that drag. An invisible band 8px above and below makes it a 21px target, 44px on a touch screen. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring, not the source's maroon one, set 5px out as the source's is so it clears the knob; the strip under it is dark in both themes, so the ring is the dark theme's accent in both (5.3:1 on it; the light accent would be 2.0:1). Empty is a clip that did not load: the track empty and the knob back at the start, as the source draws it, and also dimmed like the kit's buttons, with the plain arrow and no growth under the pointer. It is off (aria-disabled: keys and the pointer move nothing, and a drag under way is let go) but stays in the tab order, as an off pick chip does, and its value reads the reason, The clip did not load, which the words under it show (white at 60%, 7:1). A known length brings it back for the next clip. The knob is the place, 6.5:1 or more against the bar; the played part is 1.8:1 against the track, as picked, and the time beside it in the transport says the place in words. Loading is part of the clip still to come in.
- Kit note, Video player: A new kit part, Kit.videoPlayer, copied from Loss Prevention's dossier video (video.trk-media, js/argus.js:6868 and css/argus.css:10632-10642), which is unchanged. The kit draws the frame, and the video inside it is the browser's own, with its own controls: the full width up to 420px tall, the whole picture shown, on LP's sunken ground with the thin line and 12px corners, the same frame the dossier's evidence still has (--kit-still-ground, --kit-tab-line). ⛔ The browser's controls (play, the time, mute, full screen, its menu and its progress line) cannot be forced into hover, focus or a press, so in every cell they are drawn as they are at rest: default only. The forced states are what the kit draws. The frame has no hover look, as picked, so there is no hover cell; under the pointer the browser shows its own controls. Keyboard focus is the kit's shared ring round the frame, not the portal's red one; it shows while the video itself has focus, and once Tab moves on into the controls the browser draws its own ring on each. Error is a video that did not load: the source leaves a grey 0:00 player with dead controls and no word; the kit puts the words This video could not be played in the frame instead (5.3:1 in light, 7.8:1 in dark), and a video that fails later does the same. It plays https, a path on this site or a blob: URL the page made (a clip it fetched itself), and refuses anything else. Mid is the clip paused at 0:04. ⛔ No real footage: the clip is the library's own twelve-second stand-in of the empty aisle picture (assets/ui-library/scene.webm, drawn from flat shapes, served on staging only), and nothing points at evidence, storage or a tenant.

- Kit note, Card you click to open: Copied into the kit from Employees' report card (Employees Reports), which is unchanged. ⛔ Renamed kit-click-card to kit-click-box: the kit's naming guard bans the word card, because the shell repaints anything called card inside the page. The source IS repainted on its page, so its ground and edge are that paint (#242424 and a faint white line in dark, white and a faint dark line in light), which is what the owner saw; the kit states them with the plain figure's two tokens, which carry the same paint in both themes. The whole box is one control: a button, or a real link when it is given an href (then a plain click can be the page's own, and a modified one, a new tab, stays the browser's). Its name is its title, and its line of words is its description; the red Open at its foot is its look, not its name. Nothing inside it is interactive: every slot takes words, not nodes. Its title is not a heading, because a heading cannot sit inside a button; on the page the group title above the boxes is the heading. Under the pointer the kit's shadow and a 1px lift; pressed is the same, as the source has no rule of its own, and under reduced motion it does not lift. The source's hover edge and the wide box's accent tint lose to the shell's paint on its page and never show, so the kit draws neither. Keyboard focus wears the kit's shared ring (the source's is the same 2px accent, 2px out). On a touch screen it keeps its full 128px height (the touch block restates it after the 44px floor). ⛔ The picker drew it 162px tall: the scan's page wrapped it in content-box sizing, so its 128px floor measured only the inside. On Employees Reports the box is border-box and stands 128px, and the kit keeps that; Open then sits under the words rather than at the foot of a taller box, unless a taller neighbour in the row stretches it. Wide spans two columns of the page's grid with an 18px title, and one column under 640px; the grid is the page's. The title is 18.1:1 in light and 14.1:1 in dark, the line 9.4:1 and 9.5:1, the red word 11.4:1 and 7.6:1. Words are made up.
- Kit note, Details list (label and value): Copied into the kit from Employees' person drawer (its four facts), which is unchanged; the other three ways the scan found (Employees review, All stores, the roster profile) are not the pick. A bordered grid, two across, a hairline between the cells, 12px labels in the grey over 15px values, and a line under a value in the second grey. It is a real description list (each label a term, its value and its line the description) where the source is plain boxes, so a screen reader hears which label goes with which value; it looks the same. Muted is a word standing in for a value (Not set): lighter and not bold, 5.8:1 on the drawer in light and 6.8:1 in dark. A value nobody has is the kit's missing figure (Kit.missingFigure), never a blank. It opens nothing and takes no focus. The ground in the library is the drawer's. Facts are made up.
- Kit note, List box (a titled box of rows): Copied into the kit from Financials Overview's top five lists, which are unchanged; Forecast's day by day box is the same rules, and the same box holds a sentence or a chart in place of rows (the second variant). 12px corners, the kit line, the card ground, no shadow, as rendered in both themes. The head is the navigation family's section heading (Kit.sectionHeading) at the box's 16px title and 12px line, on the tinted band with a hairline under it and the total at its right. Each row is a name, a thin bar for its share and the amount, a hairline between rows; the rest row (Everything else) is in the grey with no bar. A name that goes somewhere is a real link (the source's is a button that changes the page, with a browser tooltip the kit never draws); under the pointer it underlines, 3px under the words, in both themes, as the real Financials name does (the picker's image showed no underline, which was the scan's harness, not the page), and its words keep their ink, which in light has to beat the shell, since the shell turns every link's words dark red under the pointer. Keyboard focus wears the kit's shared ring, not the source's red one. On a touch screen the name takes the 44px floor; it fills its row's name column, so it is wide enough already. Busy is the kit's loading placeholder (the feedback family's) where the total and four rows go (Financials leaves the total blank while it loads, and the picker's harness kept its figure there; the kit shows the placeholder), the box marked busy for a screen reader; it holds still under reduced motion. Empty is one sentence. A total or an amount nobody knows is the kit's missing figure (Kit.missingFigure), never a zero. The bars are the spend red for money out and the green for money in, the colours the line table already carries. On Financials the bars grow in the first time they are seen; that is the page's motion (Kit.motion.reveal), not the box's, so the kit draws them at rest. Every word clears 4.5:1 in both themes. The band of two boxes is the page's. Names and figures are made up.
- Kit note, Number or status card: Copied into the kit from Financials Insights' Money out and Summary boxes, which are unchanged. ⛔ Renamed kit-number-card to kit-number-box: the kit's naming guard bans the word card, because the shell repaints it. 12px corners, the kit line, the card ground, no shadow, 24px under its content. The title is a real heading, 24px at 500, at the level the caller picks (h2 unless told), with the total under it; it is not the section heading, because its head is a title over a figure, not a title over a sentence. The control across the box is the kit's in-page switch (the tabs family's Kit.inlineSwitch, full width); the source's is Financials' own copy of the same control. The Summary box is a two-across grid of label over value, a real description list as the source's is, with a hairline under its first row. A total the page does not know (the source's is-unknown: the figure is not available for the period) is the kit's missing figure in its lighter ink (4.88:1 on the card in light, 6.84:1 in dark, over the 3:1 a figure needs), and the note says why; a summary value nobody has is the same dash. On Financials each box stands 476px tall so two in a row line up; that height is the page's, and the picker drew them at their content's height. Under 720px the side margins go from 24px to 16px. Every word clears 4.5:1 in both themes. Figures are made up.
- Kit note, Section box: Copied into the kit from Settings' section (SettingsUI.section, on every Settings tab and Billing), which is unchanged; Settings is written in these same kit tokens. 12px corners, the kit line, the card ground, no shadow, 16px under it. The head is the navigation family's section heading (Kit.sectionHeading) at the box's own 15px title and 13px help line, its actions at the right (here the small row button). The body holds the toggles family's setting rows (Kit.settingRow), a hairline between them. Danger is a red edge and a red title (6.0:1 on the card in light, 5.3:1 in dark), never a red fill: the one red fill is the delete button inside it (the buttons family's kit-danger-warning). Quiet is the placeholder for a tab not built yet: a dashed edge, no ground and one grey sentence (5.3:1 on the page in light, 7.3:1 in dark). The box itself opens nothing and takes no focus. Words are made up.

- Kit note, Lines inside a card or dialog (no frame): Copied into the kit from Financials Insights' Top money in and out, which is unchanged. It sits in a card or a dialog and draws no frame. A row that opens something takes the pale block under the pointer, and its name is a real button, so a keyboard reaches it; the row itself is a click target for the pointer only, and a row with no name opens nothing (the kit warns). An optional hint tells a screen reader what a named row opens, as the source's hidden sentence does. The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the pale wine ring the source draws, and the source clips that ring to a sliver because its name cell hides its overflow; the kit's cell does not. The header is the lighter ink (--kit-ink-3), which is what Financials' skin makes the source's dim ink; the kit keeps the whole header that one ink, where the source's cascade darkens Amount. Loading is seven rows of the kit's loading placeholder (the feedback family's one breathing bar), held still under reduced motion (the computer's setting or Settings > Preferences). Empty keeps three still placeholder rows with the sentence over them; the source's sentence sits under its bars, which the kit fixes. A failed read shows only its sentence and Try again (the kit's everyday button). An unknown share or amount is the kit's missing-figure dash (the feedback family's one dash), named for a screen reader. The bar under % of total is the source's own and stays with the table; charts stay in their module. On a narrow screen the bar goes and the figure stays, as in Financials.
- Kit note, Main list table: The standard is the kit's existing ArgusTable, the Financials transactions table, unchanged: the owner's rule is that the Mercury table is every table's standard, and this is that table. It keeps ArgusTable's own red focus ring rather than the kit's shared one, because it is an existing kit part and is not retuned. Rows that open something take keyboard focus: Enter opens the row, the arrow keys move between rows and Space ticks the row's box. Selected is two rows ticked, which also half-ticks the select-all box. Open is the first row's Category list. Off is ArgusTable's own rule: a cell nobody can change is plain words, not a greyed box, and the first page's Previous arrow is off. Busy, empty and error are the table's three ways a read settles, which never look alike: bars, bars under a sentence, and a sentence with Try again and no rows at all. The library shows made-up rows with a fixed date and fixed amounts; it never reads real finances.
- Kit note, Table loading state: The standard is ArgusTable's own loading rows, unchanged. Default is the same table with its rows, so the bars can be read against the columns they stand in for. Busy is the real header over rows of bars at the table's own column widths and 48px pitch, breathing; the library draws five, where a table draws eight unless told otherwise. Empty is the same bars held still and fading under the sentence and a quiet action; error is the sentence and Try again, and no bars. Documents and Insights draw the same idea in their own classes today.
- Kit note, Page controls under a list: The standard is ArgusTable's own footer, unchanged: the count and two round arrows, inside the table's frame. It keeps ArgusTable's red focus ring, as an existing kit part. The arrows are real buttons named Previous page and Next page, and an arrow that cannot move is really disabled: half strength, no hover, the plain arrow cursor. Default is page two, both arrows on; off is page one, whose Previous arrow cannot go back. The footer shows only when the rows are ready.
- Kit note, Simple framed table: The kit's existing framed table, Kit.table, picked as it is and unchanged. Rows that open something take keyboard focus and the kit's shared ring, and Enter or Space opens them; only those rows light up under the pointer. A value nobody knows prints the word Unknown in the lighter ink, never a blank or a zero. Empty keeps the header and says so in one line under it. It has no sort, selection or pager of its own; a list that needs them is the list table.
- Kit note, Column sort header: The standard is ArgusTable's own sort control, unchanged, and it keeps ArgusTable's red focus ring, drawn round the label's pill. The header cell carries its sort for a screen reader (aria-sort), and the label is a real button that opens the menu, as does the Down arrow key. The menu is one pick of three: the two directions and Clear sort, which is off while nothing is sorted. The arrow keys, Home and End move in it, Escape closes it and gives focus back to the header, and Tab closes it and moves on. Selected is the table sorted by To/From, A to Z; the two-way arrow waits for the pointer or the keyboard.

- Kit note, In-page switch: Named kit-inline-switch rather than the proposed kit-in-page-switch: a kit class may not contain "-page", because the light theme repaints the headings and paragraphs inside any such class. The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the wine halo this switch draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. It picks a value, so it is a radio group, as Financials' is: the arrow keys and Home and End move the choice and the focus together, wrapping, and the switch is one tab stop. Given a panel it switches a view instead and becomes a tablist (tabs with aria-selected, the panel a tabpanel), stepping with Left and Right only. On a touch screen every segment is 44px tall and the glyph-only ones 44px wide. A glyph-only segment is named by its label for a screen reader but shows no name under the pointer yet: that hover tip comes from the kit's hover-tip standard (overlays family) when screens adopt it.
- Kit note, Main section tabs: The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the translucent red ring this row draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. A tab keeps the 6px corners of the old ring and paints nothing else, so the ring still rounds. The row scrolls sideways on a narrow screen, and a scrolling row cuts off anything that sticks out of it, so the row keeps 4px of room above and at both ends (taken back with a negative margin, so nothing moves). The whole ring shows on the first and last tab, with only its bottom edge hidden under the hairline, where the source's row cut off the ring's top and bottom. The WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with manual activation, as Financials does: Left and Right (wrapping) and Home and End move focus along the row, and Enter or Space opens the tab, because opening one starts reads. The row is one tab stop, and leaving it hands the stop back to the selected tab.
- Kit note, Side tabs: The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the wine halo this rail draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. A vertical tablist with automatic activation, as the Filters menu does: Up and Down (wrapping) and Home and End open the tab they land on, since that only swaps the pane beside the rail. The rail is one tab stop. Its panel and edge are the colours the owner saw in the picker, where it was drawn inside Financials. On a touch screen each tab is 44px tall.
- Kit note, Second-level tabs: The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the translucent red ring this row draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. Inventory's rows have no arrow keys, so the kit gives them the main tabs' keyboard: the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with manual activation (the arrows and Home and End move focus, Enter or Space opens), one tab stop. The selected tab reserves its bold width as the main tabs do, which Inventory's rows did not, so a click no longer nudges the tabs after it. The hairline is the row's own 55% line; Stock's row draws it at full strength, which is Stock's placement, not the standard. The row keeps 4px of room for the ring above and at both ends, as the main tabs do, so the whole ring shows on the first and last tab, with only its bottom edge under the hairline.

Hover is the chart scrub: a rule and a ring dot on one day, and that day's figure, date and change in the header. The library draws it through the card's own keyboard path, eleven days back from the latest; on a page the pointer moves it, and the arrow keys once the chart has focus. The badge variant is the other half of the card's hover, the source badge's tip. The tip is clipped at the card's left edge in the narrow size, as it is on Financials. The last variant is a card with one figure, no chart and an action on its floor; a chartless card takes a chart card's height from the row it stands in, which the library copies by standing it beside a hidden chart card. The first figure is the hero and hangs its minus in the margin at the width Financials does; the others sit on its baseline. A label that explains itself has the dotted underline, and its explanation is the kit's hover tip (the overlays family's, near-black in dark and near-white in light); the source used the browser's tooltip, which the kit never draws. The tip meets WCAG 1.4.13: it opens under the pointer and on focus, so a tap opens it too; it stays while the pointer moves onto it; and Escape puts it away without moving the pointer or the focus, closing only the tip. It opens above the label, where it covers no figure. The label takes keyboard focus with the kit's shared ring, and on a touch screen its 44px target is a box around it, so the figures keep their baseline. Busy is the kit's loading placeholder where each figure goes (the feedback family's breathing bar, at the headline size for the hero), and it holds still under reduced motion. Error is a read that failed: the kit's missing-figure dash and Did not load under every label. Empty is a figure nobody can give yet (an average with no full month): the same dash. The dash is the missing-figure standard (Kit.missingFigure): 4.71:1 on the page and 4.88:1 on a card in light, 7.17:1 and 6.84:1 in dark, over the 3:1 a figure needs. The 31px above the labels is the page's gap to its ruler and stays with the page. Figures are made up.
- Kit note, Figure card without a chart: Copied into the kit from Enterprise All stores' figure card, which is unchanged. The kit's name leaves out the word card on purpose: the shell repaints anything called card, so the source's ground and edge on its page are that repaint (#242424 and a faint white line in dark, white and a faint dark line in light), and the kit states them itself. It opens nothing and has no hover: the source writes a tint under the pointer, but on its page the shell's card paint beats it, so the picked card never changes under the pointer. It is not a link, takes no keyboard focus and has no pointer cursor. Empty is a figure no store has: the kit's missing-figure dash (the feedback family's, in its lighter ink), lighter in weight, on a dashed edge (the dash is the missing-figure standard, Kit.missingFigure: 4.88:1 on the card in light, 6.84:1 in dark, over the 3:1 a figure needs); the fill stays, as the picker showed it (the source asks for no fill, but the shell's paint wins on its page). The grid of cards is the page's. Figures are made up.

The kit's name leaves out the word tile on purpose: the shell repaints anything called tile. No box: a hairline on top with a short red rule at its start. One that opens its details is a real button, named for its score and status and what it opens; under the pointer the rule draws across and the arrow steps right and turns red, and keyboard focus draws the rule too, at the kit's own speeds. The ring is the kit's shared ring, not the source's red one set 4px out (the colour is the same red). Without onOpen it opens nothing and shows no arrow and no hover (the Opens nothing variant). Busy is a score still loading: a grey rule, a dash and Checking. Empty is a score with no reading yet. ⛔ Its dash is the kit's missing-figure dash (the feedback family's), in the lighter ink the words use (4.71:1 light, 7.17:1 dark), not the source's 36% ink, which is 2.2:1 on a light ground, under the 3:1 a figure this size needs: the coordinator's call under the kit's contrast rule. Every word clears 4.5:1 in both themes. A to-do count is the same figure with no unit. The four-across grid is the page's. Scores and words are made up.

- Kit note, Pick one option (radio): The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the soft wine ring round the circle this list draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere, drawn round the element that has focus, which here is the whole choice, its circle and its words. Each choice is a button the kit draws (role radio with aria-checked in a radiogroup), not the source's restyled native radio, so no browser control ships. One tab stop, the chosen choice, or the first usable one when nothing is chosen or the chosen one is off: the arrow keys (all four, wrapping) and Home and End move the choice and the focus together and skip a choice that is off (disabled or aria-disabled); Space chooses the focused one when nothing is chosen yet, and Enter does nothing, as on the platform's own radios. The group is named by its label; inside a setting row it takes the row's label, and "Options" is only the fallback. The source has no off look; the kit dims a choice that is off, as it dims its buttons, and it does not light up under the pointer. The empty circle's edge under the pointer is the pop-up's grey, since these lists open in pop-ups. On a touch screen each choice is 44px tall.
- Kit note, Setting row (a setting and its switch): The row holds the picked switch (Kit.switch) in the library, where the Settings screens hold their own; it takes any control, a tick box or a choice included, and names that control after its label when the control has no name of its own; a choice list's "Options" is only a fallback and gives way to the row's label. The hairline is between rows (none above the first), so each cell draws the row in its state with a plain row under it. Its save state is the kit's one save note, Kit.saveNote (bars__save-note), just left of the control. Busy is the row mid-save: "Saving…" beside the control and aria-busy on the row. Error is a failed save that stays until it is fixed, read out at once, with Retry. Saved fades after two seconds; the library holds it still. The source row has no off look of its own: off is the control's. On a phone the row stacks, the control under the words.
- Kit note, On/off switch: Named kit-switch beside the kit's older Kit.toggle (Settings' switch), which is unchanged. The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the soft wine halo this switch draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere. role switch with aria-checked; Space and Enter both flip it, as the source's button does. It paints no words, so its name is its label (aria-label), or the setting row it sits in names it; one left with no name warns once it is on the page. aria-disabled switches it off as surely as disabled: no click, Space or Enter gets through. The track is a child of the button rather than the button itself, so on a touch screen the button grows to 44px square around a track that stays 36 by 20. The slide takes the kit's 150ms. Off is dimmed to half, as in the source.
- Kit note, Tick box: Your rule on the empty box: it is white in light mode and grey in dark mode (--kit-tick-empty). Ticked keeps the picked look, the accent fill with the tick in the card colour. The focus ring is the kit's shared ring, not the accent ring round the box alone this tick box draws today. That is on purpose: one focus ring everywhere, drawn round the element that has focus, which is the whole tick box, its box and its words. role checkbox with aria-checked (true or false: the pick has no part-ticked look). Space ticks and unticks it; Enter does nothing, as on the platform's own tick box. The words name it and the help line describes it; one with no words and no ariaLabel warns once it is on the page, unless a setting row names it. aria-disabled switches it off as surely as disabled: no click, Space or Enter gets through. Off is dimmed to half and does not light up under the pointer. On a touch screen it is at least 44px square.
